newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/FOMC keeps investors sidelined.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/FOMC keeps investors sidelined.

text.p: Trading in major U.S. stock index options remained slow Tuesday as investors stayed on the sidelines ahead of a key announcement on interest rates, traders said.
The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee, the Federal Reserve's policy-setting unit, was meeting Tuesday and an announcement on any change in interest rates was expected around 1315 CDT/1815 GMT.
"Nobody's even playing anything. Nobody's guessing," one options broker in Chicago said. "Yesterday was super-slow and today is starting out like that."
FOMC-related nervousness put bonds and stocks under pressure, with the blue chip Dow industrial average .DJI falling 73 points to about 7156 near midday.
The S&P 500 index .SPX lost 6.61 to 826.66 and the S&P 100 index .OEX shed 6.28 to 812.18. June S&P 500 futures were off 6.75 at 829.30.
June S&P 500 fair value was pegged at roughly 2.75 points premium to cash, with arbitrage buy programs at 3.55 points over and sell programs at 1.95 points over or less.
Traders said the market could get a quick bounce later if the Fed leaves rates unchanged.
"If they don't raise rates, the market may momentarily rally, but I think we're going down both ways," the broker said.
One SPX trader said the market could rally up to its record highs if the Fed leaves rates unchanged, but that a trading range would be most likely.
"I don't really see us having a breakout like we did six weeks ago," he said. "If they raise (rates), maybe we get a swing but stay in a range over the next couple of weeks."
He said a likely range would be 15 to 20 points on S&P futures.
Traders agreed that if the FOMC raises rates by 50 basis points, the market would likely sell off sharply.
Most Fed watchers who expect an increase are looking for a 25 basis point rise.
"If they do 50 (basis points), I think this (market) will drop so fast your head will spin," the SPX options trader said.
The options broker said if the market begins to sell off after the FOMC news, selling pressure could increase through the close.
"My feeling is if they do rally, it's worth selling," he said. "And if the market starts going down, the Dow could drop below 7,000."
In volume terms, index puts were the options of choice.
By 1100 CDT/1600 GMT, SPX put volume was 33,601 compared with call volume of 13,278. In the OEX, puts outpaced calls by 10,453 to 8,187.
